title: You don’t wake up one day far from God.
paragraphs:
You don’t wake up one day far from God.
You drift… quietly.

And the scariest part?
You don’t even notice it happening.

At first, it feels small.
Harmless.
Explainable.

You tell yourself:
“I’m just tired.”
“I’ll pray later.”
“It’s not that serious.”
Because you used to feel it.

That conviction.
That fire.
That pull toward God.

Not because God stopped speaking…
But because you slowly stopped listening.

Unprayed prayers.
Unread Scriptures.
Unconfessed sin.
Unchecked thoughts.

Still showing up.
Still smiling.
Still functioning.
You remember who you used to be.

The hunger.
The tears in worship.
The urgency to obey.
It doesn’t shock you like it used to.
But that it stopped bothering you.
📖 “But exhort one another every day… that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.” — Hebrews 3:13

Until what once broke your heart…
Becomes something you tolerate.
And here’s the truth most people won’t say out loud:

You can look “fine” on the outside…
And be far from God on the inside.

You can attend church…
Post verses…
Say the right things…
📖 “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
Jesus didn’t say this to atheists.
He said it to religious people.

People who looked right…
But were far from Him.
And maybe that’s you right now.
Just not running to Him anymore.
Your private life doesn’t match your public faith.
And deep down, you feel it.
“This isn’t where I’m supposed to be.”
Because drifting doesn’t mean you’re disqualified.
It means you’re being invited back.
📖 “Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the Lord of hosts. — Malachi 3:7

“Fix yourself first.”
“Clean yourself up.”
“Earn your way back.”
That means you’re not too far.
Because this isn’t just about drifting.
It’s choosing your way over God’s way.
It’s replacing God with comfort, control, pleasure, or pride.
📖 “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
📖 “For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
But don’t stop reading the verse.
Because God didn’t leave you there.
📖 “…but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
📖 “But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not when you had it all together.
Jesus didn’t just come to make you feel better.
He lived the life you couldn’t live.
📖 “He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in His mouth.” — 1 Peter 2:22
Then He died the death you deserved.
📖 “He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
Making a way back to God.
📖 “If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.” — Romans 10:9
You don’t need a better routine.
No more pretending you’re okay when you’re not.
📖 “Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you.” — James 4:8
So let me ask you something…
Or just close to the idea of Him?
This is about grace calling you home.
The same God you drifted from…
Is the same God reaching for you.
📖 “The Lord is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love.” — Psalm 103:8
You are not too far gone.
You are not too numb to feel again.
You are not too lost to be found.
From distance to devotion — Jesus is still calling you home.
